exposure: Etiology (hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE), genetic contribution, infection, vascular etiology, metabolic etiology)
outcome: Seizure type (focal clonic, sequential, focal onset, multifocal onset)
EEG characteristics (electrographic seizures, electroclinical seizures, background EEG patterns)
Associations between etiologies/characteristics and seizure types/EEG
cohort: The study included 145 infants with neurophysiological confirmation of neonatal seizures admitted to a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit in Northern Italy between 2009 and 2022, selected from a total of 91,253 neonates.
finding: The study observed a low incidence of hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy and a high incidence of genetic etiology in their cohort of neonatal seizures, highlighting that seizure type and EEG features are fundamental in addressing etiology.
gest_age: 69.7% were born at term and 30.3% were preterm infants, with incidence of NS increasing with lower preterm age.
